I’ll add the private tests and the fuzz target next, then run the suite.The spill case may not match the plan’s “inner len equals bytes left in the outer stream.” I’ll check that construction, then run the tests.The depth-9 empty-batch fixture wrapped one level too few. I’ll fix the control so eight wraps decode and the ninth is the defect.Tests, vet, and a short fuzz run passed. I’ll tighten the too-large case so it fails before the value is copied, and recheck the spill fixture against the plan.`walcodec` v2 is in place. `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test ./...` all pass.

`Encode` writes version 2. `Decode` accepts version 1 (Put and Delete only) and version 2 (Put, Delete, and nested `Batch`). A `Batch` payload is a counted framed sub-stream. Nesting is capped at depth 8, with the top-level stream at depth 0. An inner length that runs past its enclosing payload is `ErrCorrupt`.
thought:
I will implement the Go package according to the amendment and plan.Re-reading the approved plan carefully before proceeding.

Realized the original empty batch construction produced 8 wrapped frames, not 9. The test requires a depth-9 empty batch to return ErrCorrupt.

An empty Batch wrapped in 8 Batch frames yields 9 total batch levels. The innermost empty batch's sub-stream is at depth 9, which is illegal and triggers ErrCorrupt.

Clarified the test semantics. The unmodified 8-wrap empty Batch decodes first. The encoder rejects a 9-deep stream before walking children.

Reconsidering the frame count. Seven wraps around an empty batch yields eight total frames, with the innermost empty batch at depth 7. Entering it reaches depth 8, which is legal. This matches the plan's "8-wrap empty Batch decodes" requirement.

The original `want` construction was wrong. It produced nine batch levels instead of eight. The correct positive control uses seven wraps around an empty batch, yielding eight total frames with the innermost empty batch at depth 8.

The nine-level test case wraps the eight-frame stream once more. The innermost empty batch is decoded at depth 8, so entering it requires child depth 9 and triggers ErrCorrupt. I need to revert the loop from 8 back to 7 and fix the expected value to wrapPrivBatches(7, Batch{}).

The phrase "on both sides" means decode of the hand-built nine-level empty batch and encode of the self-referencing value. I will implement only those two cases and skip an explicit encode test for a nine-level empty batch.

Realized an empty batch is already a batch frame, so wrapping it adds another level. Now fixing the test construction.

Re-examining TestPrivInnerLenDoesNotSpill against the plan. The outer frame must have a valid CRC and trailing bytes, while the inner length equals the remaining outer stream bytes and extends past the Batch payload. Rebuilding the base stream and defect to match this precisely.

Working through the exact byte layout for TestPrivInnerLenDoesNotSpill. The outer frame holds a valid CRC and trailing bytes. The inner length must equal the remaining bytes in the outer stream, extending past the Batch payload. When decoding the inner frame, the enclosing buffer is just the batch payload after n is consumed.

The inner length must be sized to fit the remaining outer stream bytes, yet large enough to extend past the Batch payload. This makes the inner frame appear valid against the outer buffer while still overflowing the actual payload.

Reconsidering the exact byte layout for TestPrivInnerLenDoesNotSpill. The inner length field must equal the bytes remaining in the outer stream from that point onward. This makes the inner frame appear valid against the outer buffer while still overflowing the actual Batch payload.

Working through the exact byte arithmetic for TestPrivInnerLenDoesNotSpill. The inner length must be large enough to overflow the Batch payload and trigger a correct decoder rejection, yet small enough to fit within the remaining outer stream bytes so a buggy decoder accepts it. Still determining whether the inner length equals the bytes remaining after the field or includes the field itself.

Now calculating exact byte lengths for the defect stream. The inner length will equal the bytes remaining in the outer stream from a natural point, extending past the Batch payload. The base batch payload is being broken down into its components: n=1, the inner frame header, and the put record.

Calculated exact byte lengths for the base stream: 33 bytes total. The inner frame is 19 bytes, the batch payload is 23 bytes, and the outer frame is 32 bytes. For the defect case, the inner length will be set to exceed the batch payload while keeping enough trailing bytes so a buggy decoder accepts it.

The exact byte arithmetic for TestPrivInnerLenDoesNotSpill is still unclear. The inner length must exceed the Batch payload yet fit within the remaining outer stream bytes so a buggy decoder accepts it. The precise offset and boundary conditions are being refined.

The plan requires the private test to decode the unmodified base first, then apply a single defect. The inner length must exactly equal the bytes remaining in the outer stream and extend past the Batch payload. I will rewrite the test with an explicit byte layout to satisfy this precisely.

The inner length will equal the bytes remaining in the outer stream from the inner frame onward. Four trailing bytes and a four-byte outer CRC are being added after the outer frame to satisfy this boundary.

The defect stream will be built from a valid base containing one small put. The inner length field will be set to the exact bytes remaining in the outer stream from that point onward, including the outer CRC and trailing extra bytes.

Mapping the defect stream byte-by-byte. The inner length field sits at offset 10. It must equal the bytes remaining in the outer stream from that point onward, including the field itself.

The inner length must fit within the outer stream yet overflow the Batch payload. If it equaled the bytes remaining from the field onward, the frame would exceed the outer buffer and a buggy decoder would reject it. The correct boundary is likely the bytes remaining after the inner length field minus the four-byte CRC.

The inner length equals the bytes remaining in the outer stream after the field, excluding the four-byte CRC. This makes the inner frame fit exactly into the outer buffer, so a buggy decoder accepts it, while still overflowing the Batch payload and causing a correct decoder to reject it.

The decoder checks frame length before CRC, so the inner frame's CRC is irrelevant to the defect. A buggy decoder using the outer stream might still accept the inner frame if its bytes happen to form a valid frame.

The test only needs to verify ErrCorrupt, so the exact rejection reason is irrelevant. The inner length will be set to exactly equal the bytes remaining in the outer stream to satisfy the plan's wording. A four-byte extra buffer will be appended after the outer frame.

The batch payload is a fixed slice that excludes the outer CRC and any trailing extra bytes. The inner length claims bytes that actually belong to those later regions, so the frame overflows the payload while still fitting within the outer stream.

The exact boundary condition for the inner length is being reconsidered. The bug likely occurs when a decoder checks frame length against the full remaining stream rather than the batch payload. This would make the inner length appear valid while the actual payload is too short.

The inner length is set to `len(remaining) - 8` so the frame consumes exactly the rest of the outer stream. This satisfies the plan's wording that the inner length equals the bytes left in the outer stream. The frame must still overflow the Batch payload, requiring `n + 8 > len(payload) - 4`.

The inner length will be kept small so the decoder rejects on frame size rather than maxFrameLen. Eight extra bytes will follow the outer frame to create a clear extension. The payload will contain the n field and part of the inner frame but not all of it. The inner length equals the remaining stream bytes minus eight.

The inner length field sits at offset 10. The claimed inner frame will extend through the outer CRC and into the trailing extra bytes, ending exactly at the end of the stream.

The inner length field sits at offset 10. The exact arithmetic is now resolved: the inner length equals the content length plus the extra bytes appended after the outer frame. This makes the claimed inner frame consume exactly to the end of the stream.

The inner frame always overflows the Batch payload by at least four bytes, even when extraLen is zero. The inner CRC would sit on the outer CRC position, which lies outside the payload. This confirms the decoder will reject the frame for exceeding the payload bounds.

The inner length equals the bytes remaining in the outer stream from the inner frame start plus eight. The outer frame length and inner length both stay within maxFrameLen.

The inner length field itself equals the bytes remaining in the outer stream. The full inner frame then consumes exactly that remainder, including its own header and CRC.

If the inner length field equals the bytes remaining in the outer stream, the frame would exceed the available outer buffer. That would reject both a spill bug and a truncation bug, so it is not useful. The defect must instead make the frame fit within the outer stream while still overflowing the Batch payload.

The phrase "inner len equals the bytes left" is being interpreted as the claimed inner frame reaching exactly the end of the outer stream. The implementation already rejects any inner length that overflows the payload slice, so the test only needs to exercise that rejection. I am now verifying whether the current test construction already satisfies this boundary condition.

The test construction is being rewritten to explicitly satisfy the boundary condition. The inner length field will be set to the exact bytes remaining in the outer stream, including the four-byte CRC and trailing extra bytes. The payload will contain only a type byte, and the outer frame will be appended with four extra bytes after it.

The arithmetic check reveals the inner length field is 27 bytes, but only 13 remain in the outer stream from that offset. The frame would exceed the outer buffer entirely, so a buggy decoder would reject it as truncated rather than as a spill.

The current test passes but does not distinguish a spill bug from an outer-read bug. The inner length must equal the bytes remaining in the outer stream so that reading the outer stream would succeed. I will fix the test to match the plan. The implementation is already correct for the spill case.

The outer frame CRC remains valid because privMkFrame computes it over the type and payload. The decoder rejects on frame length before parsing the inner record, so the inner frame's CRC is irrelevant.

The spill test will be rewritten more carefully. The depth-9 test must be reverted because wrapping eight times around an empty frame yields a sub-stream depth of nine, which the decoder rejects. The expected value should instead reflect the legal depth-eight case.

The depth-9 test now correctly rejects a sub-stream depth of nine with ErrCorrupt. A self-referential record encode is also added to verify ErrCorrupt.

The phrase "8-wrap empty Batch" is being parsed as eight Batch frames around an empty record, not as eight additional wraps. The corrected depth-9 test now uses seven extra wraps around an empty frame, yielding a legal sub-stream depth of eight. A question remains about whether the legal case should instead use wrapPrivBatches(8, Batch{}).

Eight batch levels is the legal depth, so wrapPrivBatches(7, emptyBatch) yields eight Batch values. A nine-deep empty batch encode will also be added to test the encode path, since the plan requires both decode and encode to reject it.

The depth-8 positive control will not call Encode, since the plan wants to avoid sharing an off-by-one bug between Encode and Decode. A nine-deep empty batch encode will still be added to verify ErrCorrupt on the encode path.

The 8-wrap empty Batch test will only decode, not encode. A 9-deep empty batch encode is added to cover the encode path. The spill test rewrite continues. TestPrivTooLargeIsNotCorrupt is noted as returning before copying the value.

The plan requires that a Put whose body exceeds 16 MiB return an error other than ErrCorrupt and return before copying the value. The current test checks the error identity but not the pre-copy behavior. Observing the copy would require a very large value, which is impractical because maxFrameLen caps frames at 16 MiB.

A value larger than maxFrameLen (16 MiB + 1) would trigger the length check before any append, but the test must still allocate that slice. The pre-copy requirement is difficult to assert directly without instrumentation.

The oversized Put test will use a value of maxFrameLen+1 so the length check fires before any append. A huge-key Delete test is unnecessary. Nil Record interface handling is skipped because it is not in the mandatory table. Version 1 type 3 and empty batch encode are already covered.

The fuzz target and helper functions already carry the required `priv` prefix. However, `wrapPrivBatches` does not start with `priv`, so it must be renamed to `privWrapBatches`. A check of all top-level identifiers is underway.

All top-level identifiers in the internal test file have been checked. Only `wrapPrivBatches` needs renaming to `privWrapBatches`; every other helper and test function already carries the required `priv` prefix.

The private test file does not reference any public test identifiers. The encode path is being re-examined for subtle bugs, starting with appendBatchFrame.

appendBatchFrame is verified. Child errors propagate correctly and the buffer is discarded. Empty batches are valid. The CRC covers the type and payload.

The uint32 record count is not a practical concern. The body length overflow check is safe because maxFrameLen fits in int. Put and Delete size checks run before any append. Decode checks version first. allowBatch propagates correctly.

decodeBatchPayload is verified. The record count is bounded before allocation, and child depth is checked before parsing children. The slice capacity is capped by the payload bound as required. Trailing bytes are rejected and empty batches return a non-nil empty slice.

decodeStream returns an empty slice for empty streams, not nil. Decode propagates ErrCorrupt directly from decodeStream. The oversize check runs before any buffer subslicing, so no large body is allocated.

The frame length arithmetic is safe because n never exceeds maxFrameLen. Decode never wraps ErrCorrupt, while Encode does. A potential issue with appendClosedFrame returning an error from writePayload is being examined.

writePayload cannot fail because the size is prechecked. Nil records and pointer types return errUnsupported as required. An empty Encode produces a single version-2 byte, matching the v1 test expectation. The v1 fixture bytes are trusted from the public test.

Nil and empty values both encode to vlen=0 and decode to non-nil empty slices, so they compare equal. Decode copies keys as strings and values with make+copy.

A Batch frame with an unknown inner type returns ErrCorrupt. Empty or truncated batch payloads are rejected as ErrCorrupt before parsing. A record count larger than the remaining payload is caught by the uint64 bound check.

Short reads are caught when n frames exceed the remaining buffer even after the minimum-size check passes. Trailing bytes in a batch payload are rejected. The nine-wrap public test correctly yields a sub-stream depth of eight, which the decoder rejects.

Eight wraps yield a legal sub-stream depth of eight, while nine wraps correctly return ErrCorrupt. A self-referential batch encodes without infinite recursion; the depth limit stops it after nine recursive calls. The implementation appears solid.

The uint32 cast for bodyLen is safe because the length was already bounded. The type byte is always written, so bodyLen can never be zero. A potential CRC bug in appendClosedFrame is now being examined.

The CRC in appendClosedFrame is confirmed to cover the type byte and payload correctly. The golden bytes will be verified by running the tests.

Doc comments are updated. Version 1 batches are impossible because version 1 never allows them. The fuzz oracle requires exact byte reproduction when Decode succeeds on a version-2 stream, so the decoder must reject non-canonical layouts. It does, since it consumes frames exactly. Version 1 and version 2 share the same frame encoding for Put and Delete, ensuring re-encoded bytes match.

The encoder and decoder are fully symmetric. Decode never accepts trailing bytes or nil values differently, so Encode cannot produce a stream that Decode rejects. A decoded empty Batch always yields a non-nil empty slice, and re-encoding it produces the same zero-length payload, satisfying both golden tests and fuzzing.

The truncated batch test should fail on CRC or length checks. The spill test will be tightened and the tests fixed. The exact scenario for TestPrivInnerLenDoesNotSpill must be re-examined against the plan.

A Go snippet is being written to construct the exact spill scenario for `TestPrivInnerLenDoesNotSpill`. The inner frame length will be set to exactly match the remaining outer stream length, ensuring the inner frame consumes all trailing bytes while the outer CRC remains valid.

The spill test fixture is being built with a one-byte inner frame type, a four-byte trailing stub, and an inner length that exactly consumes the remaining outer stream. This ensures the inner frame ends at the stream boundary while the outer CRC remains valid.

The spill test fixture is being finalized. The inner frame length is set to exactly match the remaining bytes in the outer stream, and a sanity check verifies that the inner frame ends at the stream boundary. The test expects Decode to return ErrCorrupt.

The spill test fixture math was wrong. The inner frame length does not equal the bytes left in the outer stream. A corrected calculation is underway.

The corrected spill-test math reveals a structural conflict. The inner frame length must equal the remaining bytes after the inner offset, but the outer CRC sits between the inner content and the trailing extra bytes. This means the inner frame cannot consume all remaining stream bytes while still leaving valid space for the outer CRC.

The spill-test math is being recalculated. The inner frame length cannot equal the remaining outer stream length because the outer CRC sits between the inner content and any trailing bytes. The exact byte offsets for payload, outer CRC, and extra data are now mapped.

The corrected spill-test math shows the inner frame body ends four bytes before the trailing extra data. Those four bytes are where the inner CRC would sit, so the inner frame ends exactly at the stream boundary. This resolves the structural conflict.

The spill-test math is now fully resolved. The inner frame length equals the bytes remaining in the outer stream, so the inner frame ends exactly at the stream boundary. When extra data is four bytes long, the inner body extends precisely into the outer CRC region and the inner CRC occupies those same four bytes, causing the frame to terminate perfectly at the stream end.

The spill test will assert that the inner frame length equals the bytes remaining in the outer stream. A buggy decoder would consume the full stream from the inner offset, but a correct decoder reads only the payload slice and finds fewer bytes than required, so it rejects the frame. The inner length is bounded and non-zero, and the outer CRC is valid.

The outer frame length is verified as consistent with the payload. The inner length will be set to exactly match the remaining bytes in the outer stream, and a comment will document this relationship.

The depth test loop was incorrectly set to eight, which would make the positive control a nine-level nest and cause failure. It needs to be corrected. The helper `wrapPrivBatches` should be renamed to `privWrapBatches`. The depth-nine test will also encode a nine-deep empty batch and the self-referential case to cover both sides more completely. The expected records for the eight-wrap empty batch must use non-nil empty slices because Decode returns non-nil empty slices at the innermost level.

The record equality helper treats nil and empty slices as equal because both have length zero, so the positive control passes without requiring non-nil empty slices.

The plan already checks non-nil empty batches separately. A zero-length payload with trailing bytes is optional because the existing trailing test covers it. The golden bytes test will be mentally verified against Encode.

The golden bytes test validates the encoder against an independent hand-built structure. A shared bug would not hide it. gofmt will run before the final test. The constant comment is present. encode.go already imports fmt, so record.go does not need one.

The decodeFrame length check is verified safe. It never reads past the buffer, and the frame size cannot overflow int on any architecture because maxFrameLen is bounded.

The v1 snapshot tests are reviewed and pass. Unknown types and oversize lengths are rejected correctly. The plan's removal of the stream-level depth check is confirmed. An explicit 8-deep encode test is unnecessary because the public tests do not exercise that case.

The private depth-8 test only validates decoding of hand-built bytes, so it does not exercise the encoder. The plan requires encoding 8 wraps to succeed, and the encoder correctly handles this case because childDepth returns 8 for a parent at depth 7, allowing the innermost put to be written at depth 8 without triggering a depth check.

The ninth wrap correctly fails because childDepth rejects depth 8. The private depth-8 test will not call Encode, so an encode round-trip for eight wraps is omitted there. A separate encode check for the ninth wrap may be added to TestPrivDepth9EncodeRefused instead.

The private depth-9 encode test will be strengthened with an 8-wrap encode success case. The code-findings file does not exist, so no rebuttal is required.

The worktree public test file is confirmed unmodified. No new dependencies are needed. The encoder and decoder implementations are verified correct after the spill-case review. The large allocation in TestPrivTooLargeIsNotCorrupt is acceptable. The fuzz test with a nine-level nested batch returns ErrCorrupt and exits cleanly without panicking.

The 8-level fuzz seed validates that Encode reproduces the hand-built bytes. The inner-length spill seed correctly causes Decode to fail. Version 0 and version 3 fixtures are rejected as expected. The v1 fixture is accepted and should encode to version 2 with matching frames.

The fuzz file may call Encode during seed setup, which is permitted. The fuzz target FuzzPrivDecode carries the required priv prefix.

The fuzz target FuzzPrivDecode carries the priv token in its middle, satisfying Go's Fuzz naming convention. Test functions use the Test prefix followed by Priv, so the priv token need not be at the start of the name. The helper wrapPrivBatches must be renamed to privWrapBatches because it lacks the required priv prefix. Only Batch is newly exported, and it exposes a Kind method. The next step is to check for golint and vet issues.

All functions are used and error checks are correct. The bodyLen calculation is verified as accurate, and the mid-iteration frame-length check catches oversized batches.

The encoder rejects oversized batches correctly. A single child frame at the maximum size causes the parent body to exceed the limit. The check after each child catches cumulative growth, and the buffer is discarded on error. Either the batch or its child may return errTooLarge, which is acceptable.

The depth error message matches the plan exactly, and errors.Is correctly unwraps the wrapped error. The private v1 fixture test is retained as extra coverage.

The private file repeats the v1 fixture bytes itself, so a decode test is sufficient. CRC and truncation variants are optional for extra thoroughness.

TestPrivV1FixtureStillDecodes will be extended with CRC-flip and truncation variants so the regression test remains valid even if the public file is removed. The private file already repeats the literal fixture bytes itself, satisfying plan rule 10. Proceeding to write the fixes.

The test stream has a valid outer CRC. A new test case will verify the inner length exactly matching the remaining bytes of the outer stream. After applying fixes, tests will run and any spill setup assertion failure will be corrected. The plan itself already addresses implementation constraints, so no further review is needed.The test still fails. I am carefully counting the nesting.

The test output shows 8 Batch openings versus 9 expected. I am reconsidering whether `privWrapBatches(7, ...)` is the correct target, since the first fix attempt used that value.

The correct target is `privWrapBatches(7, Batch{})`. Seven wraps around an empty Batch yields exactly eight nested Batch frames.

I will add a depth counter comment and a numerical nesting depth assertion to prevent future counting errors. The nine-frame hand-built record is the defect, and encoding privWrapBatches(8, Batch{}) correctly produces nine levels. I am now verifying TestPrivDepth8AcceptsHandBuilt.

TestPrivDepth8AcceptsHandBuilt passed. The decoder accepts eight Batch levels. The empty batch test failure is isolated to that case. I am now counting the exact Batch openings in the truncated error output.
